terms.home rule: A city of more than 5,000 people in Texas may adopt its own charter by a vote of its residents. That charter, rather than general state law alone, sets how the city governs itself. Copperas Cove is a home rule city.
terms.general law city: A Texas city that has not adopted its own charter. It may only do what state law specifically allows. The opposite of a home rule city.
terms.charter: The city's founding document. It works somewhat like a local constitution, setting the powers of the council, the mayor, the city manager and residents.
terms.charter amendment: A change to the charter. In Texas it takes a majority of the voters who vote at an election held for that purpose.
terms.ordinance: A local law passed by the city council. It carries penalties and stays in effect until repealed.
terms.resolution: A formal statement or decision by the council. Generally used for administrative matters and does not carry the force of a local law the way an ordinance does.
terms.quorum: The minimum number of members who must be present for a body to legally conduct business.
terms.canvass: The official process of reviewing and certifying election results. The canvass, not election-night reporting, is the authoritative record of what passed.
terms.initiative: A petition process letting residents put a proposed ordinance on the ballot.
terms.referendum: A petition process letting residents force a public vote on an ordinance the council already passed.
terms.recall: A petition process letting residents force an election on removing an elected official before the end of their term.
terms.forfeiture of office: Losing a seat automatically or by hearing for violating a condition in the charter, such as missing too many meetings. Different from recall, because residents do not vote on it.
terms.bond: Money borrowed by the city, repaid over years with interest.
terms.general obligation bond: Borrowing generally repaid using tax-supported revenue. Depending on the legal structure, some general obligation debt requires voter approval.
terms.certificate of obligation: A borrowing method available to Texas cities that in many cases does not require a bond election, though it carries notice requirements and a petition right for residents. Legal requirements vary and should be checked against the current statute.
terms.revenue bond: Borrowing repaid from the revenue of a specific city system, such as water or sewer, rather than from general taxes.
terms.refunding bond: New borrowing issued to pay off older borrowing, usually to lower the interest cost.
terms.debt service: The annual cost of paying back what the city has borrowed, principal plus interest.
terms.tax rate: The rate applied to property value to fund the city. Texas law sets thresholds above which an increase may require voter approval.
terms.city manager: The appointed chief administrator who runs city departments day to day. Not elected. Appointed by and serving under the council.
terms.council-manager government: A structure where residents elect a council, and the council appoints a professional manager to run daily operations.
terms.public information request: A request under the Texas Public Information Act for records held by a government body.
terms.open meetings: The Texas Open Meetings Act requires most government business to be conducted in meetings open to the public, with posted notice.
